related_questions.question: How do you find out if you have an autoimmune disease?

text_blocks.snippet: To find out if you have an autoimmune disease, you should first be aware of potential symptoms and then consult with a healthcare professional. They will likely perform a physical exam, discuss your health history, and order specific blood tests like ANA (antinuclear antibody) tests or other autoantibody tests to look for markers of autoimmune activity. Imaging tests like X-rays or MRIs might also be needed in some cases.
snippet_highlighted_words: first be aware of potential symptoms and then consult with a healthcare professional

list.title: 1. Be aware of symptoms:
list.snippet: Autoimmune diseases can manifest in various ways, but common symptoms include:
Joint pain and stiffness: Especially in the morning or after inactivity.
Skin rashes: Including those with redness, itching, or scaling.
Digestive issues: Such as bloating, cramping, diarrhea, or constipation.
Other symptoms: Fever, swollen glands, muscle pain, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating.

list.title: 2. Consult a healthcare provider:
list.snippet: If you experience persistent symptoms, especially if they are new or unusual for you, schedule an appointment with your doctor. They can help determine if your symptoms are related to an autoimmune disease.

list.title: 3. Undergo a physical exam and discuss your health history:
list.snippet: Your doctor will assess your symptoms and ask about your medical history, including family history of autoimmune diseases.
ANA (Antinuclear Antibody) Test: This test looks for antibodies that attack the nucleus of your cells, which is a common indicator of autoimmune diseases.
Autoantibody Tests: These tests look for specific antibodies that target particular tissues or organs, helping to identify the specific autoimmune disease.
CBC (Complete Blood Count) with WBC Differential: This test can help identify inflammation and abnormalities in blood cell counts.

Other tests: Depending on your symptoms and initial test results, your doctor might order other tests like ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate), CRP (C-reactive protein), or imaging tests (X-rays, MRI, etc.).

list.title: 5. Differential Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Autoimmune diseases can be tricky to diagnose because symptoms often overlap with other conditions. Your doctor will rule out other potential causes before confirming an autoimmune disease diagnosis.

list.title: 6. Follow-up:
list.snippet: If an autoimmune disease is suspected, your doctor will discuss treatment options and ongoing management strategies. It's important to follow up with your doctor regularly to monitor your condition and adjust treatment as needed.
